links.reason: The goad (தோட்டி) of Kural 24 and the five elephants (ஐங்களிற்றின் ஆட்டுண்டு) of Elathi 11 are one figure for the five senses, and item 3 (அவாஅறான்) is the clause that carries it. Reading புழை as rebirth is an inference, but the teaches claim that Elathi shows the uncontrolled case the couplet leaves out holds.

நசைகொல்லா and நசையழுங்க share the image of an asker's hope dying, so the link is real. But Naladiyar's point is the distinction between honest refusal (இல்லென்றல் வசையன்று) and false delay, and Iniyavai line 1 makes no such distinction, so the quatrain is not developed. This is a shared virtue with a shared word.

The two verses share the phrase இயைவது கரத்தல் / இயைவ கரப்பான். Muthumozhikkanchi 55 classes it as the greatest கொடுமை and Thirikadugam 45 sends it to நிரயம், so the pair does name both the kind and the fate, and the measure இயைவது limits both to what one can give.

Elathi 8 opens with உடன்படான் கொல்லான, two separate acts, and Sirupanchamoolam 69 counts கொலையை உடன்பட்டான் as one of the five who share the sin. The pairing shows consent counted as its own act, a sin in one verse and its refusal a merit in the other, which neither verse shows alone.

Thirikadugam 80 names the missing condition (நெஞ்சில் நிறையிலான் கொண்ட தவம்), which turns the Kural's circular தவமுடையார்க்கு ஆகும் into a condition. By the brief's rule that makes it qualifies, not agrees. The list does group three gains wasted on unfit holders (தூற்றின்கண் தூவிய வித்து), though 'ranks' overstates it.

Line 8 (கற்றலின் கற்றாரை வழிபடுதல் சிறந்தன்று) ranks service above learning, and line 93 (கற்றல் வேண்டுவோன் வழிபாடு தண்டான்) makes it what the learner never drops. The pair does show வழிபாடு as both end-ranking value and means, a real link within the book.
links.text_issue: The packet flags verse 8 as differing from the site's text (similarity 0.28), so its numbering or reading may not be settled.

links.reason: Both verses set wife, servant and kin as afflictions, so the connection is real, and the named item 3 (செயிர்நிற்கும் சுற்றமும்) carries only part of it. The teaches claim that Thirikadugam 'adds old age' is false: மயிர்நரைப்ப marks the time of the devouring and is not a fourth item.
links.text_issue: Sirupanchamoolam 61 line 1 (அடங்காய், பெண்வியக்க) is hard, so the identity of its first three figures is uncertain.

links.reason: Both verses count a guest among things அரிய, but in different senses: 69's lost guest (நெறிமாறி வந்த விருந்து) is பெறுமாறு அரிய, hard to come by, while 76's rainy-day guest is போற்றற்கு அரியார், hard to tend. 76 does not limit 69's claim, so qualifies fits loosely, and 'the hardest burden' overstates அரிய.
links.text_issue: Thirikadugam 76 line 1 reads வருந்தும்; the count and tamilvu want விருந்தும், and the link rests on that emendation.

links.reason: Both lines condemn reproaching the small (சிறியோர் ஒழுக்கம் ... பழியார்; குற்றமே கூறி விடும்), but the reasons differ. The பழியார் ten excuses faults by circumstance (29 வறியோன் வள்ளியன் அன்மை பழியார், 28 the customs of an unknown land), while Kural 980 praises greatness that hides another's அற்றம். The teaches claim that restraint is 'hardest and most telling' on the small is in neither text.

Thirikadugam 43 sets செய்கை அடங்குதல் திப்பியமாம் below நெஞ்சம் அடங்குதல் வீடாகும், so the Kural's single reward of அடக்கம் (அமரருள் உய்க்கும்) becomes the middle rung under release. Item 2 is the right item, and the rising order mouth, deed, heart is in the verse.

In பேணில் ஈகை மாற்றலின் துவ்வாது, a gift without regard is no better than refusal, and this is the giver's side of Kural 1057's joy at இகழ்ந்தெள்ளாது ஈவார். The துவ்வாது ten does set it beside 33 நாணில் வாழ்க்கை and 36 பொய்வேளாண்மை, outward forms without substance, as list_adds says.

Kural 19 makes தவம் depend on rain (வானம் வழங்காதெனின்), and item 2 of Nanmanikkadigai 47 makes rain depend on ascetics (மழையும் தவமிலார் இல்வழி இல்லை). Together they close a real circle, and the verse's chain does end in இல்வாழ்வார்.

Both lists do open with the chaste wife (கற்புடைய பெண்ணமிர்து; அருந்ததிக் கற்பினார் தோளும்). But Thirikadugam 1's other two items are company and learned friends, not 'public goods of the realm', so the teaches claim is false for one of the two verses, and amrita (அமிர்து) is not the same predicate as medicine (மருந்து).

Elathi 27 assigns வெஃகல், வெகுடல், தீக்காட்சி to the mind (உள்ளத்த ஆக உரை), and two of them overlap with Kural 35's அவா and வெகுளி. Elathi doesn't limit the Kural; it re-sorts the faults by faculty, so qualifies is the wrong type. The claim that the Kural 'keeps to passions' ignores its இன்னாச்சொல்.
links.text_issue: Elathi 27 lines 1 and 3 (அஃகுநீ, கள்ளத்த அல்ல) are obscure.

links.reason: Kural 159 praises bearing (நோற்கிற்பவர்) harsh words, while Thirikadugam 48 has one take abuse as sweet speech (வைதலை இன்சொல்லாக் கொள்வான்) and calls this மெய்ப்பொருள் கண்டு. The two grades, enduring and no longer tasting the bitter, are real, and the food items do make it a general reversal of taste.

The dance names do recur (கொடுகொட்டி, பண்டரங்கம்; கொடிகட்டி பாண்டுரங்), which is a real shared vocabulary. But the claim that Tirumanthiram places these dances 'in the nadis' rests on an unclear line 2, and Kalittokai is not 'the oldest love anthology'. That the later list 'inherited a performance repertoire, not a private vision' is not shown by either text.
links.text_issue: Tirumanthiram 2733 reads கொடிகட்டி for கொடுகொட்டி, and its lines 2 and 3 are syntactically unclear.

links.reason: Purananuru 143's question யார்கொல் அளியள் goes unanswered, and in 144 the woman answers (யாம் அவன் கிளைஞரேம் அல்லேம்) and names the cause (எம்போல் ஒருத்தி நலன்நயந்து). Same patron, same scene, two poets, so the claim of a cycle built up in turn holds as a reading of the sequence.

Item 4 (ஊடல்சாம் ஊடல் உணரார் அகத்து) and Kural 1308 (in the புலவி chapter: no use suffering without a காதலர் who knows it) both place the life of the lover's quarrel in the partner's understanding. The verse's other three items (நன்றி, விருந்து, பாடல்) do extend this to a general rule of the unfit receiver.

Akananuru 233 names உதியஞ் சேரல் பெருஞ்சோறு கொடுத்த ஞான்றை and turns the gathered கூளிச் சுற்றம் into a simile for crowded hills, and Purananuru 2 praises பெருஞ்சோற்று மிகுபதம் வரையாது கொடுத்தோய். The two meet on a specific act of a named patron, so the inference that this puram fame was common knowledge holds.
links.text_issue: Purananuru 2 names the patron only in its colophon; the poem itself names the feast.

links.reason: Kural 542 has the people live looking to the king's கோல், and Sirupanchamoolam 45 runs the dependence upward (வரம்புயர ... குடியுயர ... கோவுயரும்). Item 5, the king's rise as last effect, carries the qualification. The ladder is in the verse.

Both verses share முழுமக்கள் and இனம் (கல்விக்கு அகன்ற இனம்புகுவான்; பெருமையுடையார் இனத்தின் அகறல்), so the link is real. But company is only one item of three in each, and the verse defines the fool also by killing and squandered wealth. 'The first test of folly' is not claimed by the book.

Elathi 73 does call மனைவாழ்க்கை and மாதவம் both மாண்ட வினைவாழ்க்கை. But Kural 46 asks only what a virtuous householder gains by the புறத்தாறு, and it does not disparage renunciation, so Elathi is not 'declining the Kural's ranking'. The named item 2 is arbitrary, since the claim rests on the pair, and the definitions by பற்று rest on obscure lines 3 and 4.
links.text_issue: Elathi 73 line 4 (பற்றுதல் பாத்தில் தவம்) is obscure.

links.reason: Kural 19 says தானம் தவம் need rain, and Kural 34 says the whole of அறன் is a spotless mind, with outward show ஆகுல நீர. The two are compatible, since 34 would itself count the outward practices of 19 as show. The note names no reading on which the claims conflict.

Elathi 29's களவு and காமத்தீ வாழ்க்கை overlap Sirupanchamoolam 18's கள்ளாமை and மெல்லியலார் வையாமை, and 18 adds the reward of release (பேர்த்துடம்பு கோடல் அரிது). But 18 also includes பொய்யாமை, a fault of speech, so it is not a 'bodily code', and the link is largely shared virtue words.
links.text_issue: Sirupanchamoolam 18 வையாமை and நையாமை are uncertain.

links.reason: Both verses measure an act against sacrifice (வேள்வியோடு ஒப்ப; ஆயிரம் வேட்டலின் ... நன்று), and the contrast drawn is accurate. But the acts differ (வேளாண்மை vs not killing), and neither verse limits the other, so qualifies doesn't fit. The pairing rests on a shared standard of comparison.

Line 20 does keep செய்கை as the sign of ஆண்மை, and the அறிவுப் பத்து gives other signs (11 ஈரம் for birth, 12 ஈகை for ஈரம்). But the other signs are themselves deeds (12 ஈகை, 13 உதவி), so the ten does not set deeds aside as one test among several. That undercuts list_adds and makes the qualification of Kural 505's கருமமே thin.

Kural 2 ties the fruit of learning to worship (வாலறிவன் நற்றாள் தொழாஅர் எனின்), and Elathi 64 orders taking the Exalted one as lord, then his book, restraint and penance, ending in வீடு. Item 1 is first in the verse's order, and the pair does turn the binding of learning to worship into stages of a path. 'Ranked' in list_adds means 'ordered'.

The verbal echo is strong (அவாவினை ... தவாவினை; தவாவாம் அவாவிலார் செய்யும் வினை), and item 4 is the right item. But item 4 restates the couplet, so the relation is agrees. The claim that this shows why the condition is 'hardest for the one who already has' is an inference neither verse makes, and it rests on an uncertain line 3.
links.text_issue: Nanmanikkadigai 67 lines 1 to 3 are dense, and the parse of அவாவாம் அடைந்தார்கட்கு உள்ளம் is uncertain.

links.reason: Kural 890 (உடம்பாடு இலாதவர் வாழ்க்கை, a snake in the hut, in the chapter on inner enmity) leaves the discordant housemates unnamed, and Sirupanchamoolam 61 names five (கிளை, பெண், தொண்டு, மகன், அயல்) and calls them a disease (உள்ளநோய் வேண்டா). The roster point holds even with the uncertain portraits.
links.text_issue: Sirupanchamoolam 61 line 1 is hard, and கரம் may mean poison.

links.reason: அருள் and இருள் உலகம் are shared (அருள்சேர்ந்த நெஞ்சினார்; அருள்புரிந்து சொல்லுக சொல்லை ... இருள்உலகம் சேராத ஆறு). Item 3 carries the grace of the heart into speech, and the verse adds wealth for giving and books for dharma. The teaches claim is true and specific.

Both verses argue against theft by its outcome (கடிய வருதலால்; விளைவின்கண் வீயா விழுமம்), so the narrow pairing holds. But the generalisation that 'the ethics books argue by outcome, not by rule' is false of Nanmanikkadigai 86 itself, whose four வேண்டும் are rules and only the first has a reason. So the other three are not 'ways of making trouble for oneself'.

On the reading of வருத்தம் as effort, வாழாமல் வருந்தியது வருத்தம் அன்று refuses to count fruitless strain, while Kural 619 promises மெய்வருத்தக் கூலி even when the goal fails. These are opposed claims about the same case, a tension rather than a qualification. The அல்ல ten does set it beside 48 giving and 49 penance.
links.text_issue: Muthumozhikkanchi 47 is open to a second reading (deserved grief), which the marker flags.

links.reason: Naladiyar 123 makes leprosy the return of the old deed (பழவினை வந்தடைந்தக்கால்), and Sirupanchamoolam 75 makes present health the return of past healing (முன்னாளில் தீர்த்தாரே இந்நாள் ஒருநோயும் இன்றி). The two show the same law of disease as karmic fruit running both ways.
links.text_issue: The disease names in Sirupanchamoolam 75 (சிக்கர், துக்கர், துருநாமர்) are rare and uncertain.

links.reason: Kural 720 measures the waste of the speech (அங்கணத்துள் உக்க அமிழ்து), and Nanmanikkadigai 97 item 3 the loss of standing to the learned speaker (கற்றான் ஒருவனும் பாடிலனே கல்லாதார் ... முன்னர்ப் படின்). It mirrors item 2 (கல்லாதான் in a fit அவை), so the mismatch fails both ways.

The two sister works share backbiting (நட்டார்ப் புறங்கூறான்; முன்னை யுரையார் புறமொழிக் கூற்று), one as இனிது and one as இன்னா. Innaa 32 does not say whose pain it is, so 'the victim's pain' against 'the speaker's restraint' is supplied. This is a shared vice word in two mirror books.
links.text_issue: Iniyavai 19 line 1 வாழ்தால் is a misprint for வாழ்தல்.

links.reason: Sirupanchamoolam 63 conditions the fruit on சிறுபயம் என்னார், setting size aside, and 64 names the melted heart (உள்நெகிழ்ந்து ஈயின் சிறிதெனினும் குன்றுபோற் கூடும் பயன்) as the measure. Read in sequence, the second does develop the first.
links.text_issue: Sirupanchamoolam 63 பின்னிறை and சிதவலிப்பு are uncertain.

links.reason: Item 4 (கொள்ளாமை வேண்டும் பகை) and Kural 871 (பகை ... நகையேயும் வேண்டற்பாற்று அன்று) share a ban on enmity. Beyond the jest clause the pairing adds little, and 'with anyone at all' depends on attaching யார்மாட்டும் to line 4, which the marker says is open, so teaches mostly restates the shared virtue.

Nanmanikkadigai 33 states a birth-rank as fact (அந்தணரின் நல்ல பிறப்பில்லை), and the Siddhar verse denies that birth leaves any mark on the body (இறைச்சிதோல் எலும்பினும் இலக்கமிட்டு இருக்குதோ). Both speak of rank by birth between the two ends of the order, and the note treats the rule historically. The Siddhar's பணத்தி as brahmin woman is traditional.
links.text_issue: Siddhar 1003 பணத்தி is read as the brahmin woman by tradition only.

links.reason: அறனை நினைப்பானை அல்பொருள் அஞ்சும் does make the Kural's act of letting go (அன்றே யொழிய விடல்) a property of the person, and item 2 is right. But list_adds calls the three 'a ranking of inner strengths': the verse does not rank them, and the warrior's மறம் feared by எவ்வுயிரும் is not an inner strength like the other two.

Both verses concern the ploughman, so there is a connection. But 49's ruins (பொச்சாப்பு, பொருட்செருக்கு, முற்றாமை, முரண், quarrel with the தொழில்மகன்) are not 'answered item by item' by 59's straw, cattle, tools, manure and plough; only negligence matches care.
links.text_issue: Sirupanchamoolam 59 lines 1 and 3 (மா டோ, என்றிலை) are doubtful.

links.reason: Sirupanchamoolam 43 seeks the reckoner of five astrological parts for fixing the day of தோள்கூட்டல், and Naladiyar 52 mocks those who பிதற்றும் astrology endlessly instead of minding death. These are different cases, the householder consulting and the scholar who never stops, so 'disagree on the worth of the same craft' overstates. The note also names no reading on which they conflict.

Naladiyar 65 says the gift of one without wealth (கிளைபொருள் இல்லான் கொடையே) is the true gift, and Iniyavai 22 calls வருவாயறிந்து வழங்கல் sweet. These are compatible, since the poor man may give within his means. The quatrain does not prize a gift that 'strains one's means', so 'the ethics group divided' is not shown. The list does group three kinds of self-measure.
links.text_issue: Iniyavai 22 line 2 reads பங்கு where tamilvu has பாங்கு.

verses.note: No count word; the six gifts to those who live by learning are read from lines 1-2, and பேண் and எண்ணும் எழுத்திலை are uncertain.
Only four predicates governed by the final இல் are found, not five or six: no one knows all, no one knows nothing, no one is faultless, no one has learned every branch.
கண்கண்பட்டு ஆழ்ந்து நெகிழ்ந்தவர் is read as the giver's melted pity, not a sixth recipient.
Only three gain-and-means pairs are named (gift to enjoyment, penance to heaven, unattached penance to release), not five or six; lines 1-2 are framing.
A prefatory verse naming the book; the five are read from lines 1-2, and line 2 (இவையல வோர்நாலிட்டு) is obscure.
The five are read as the two ways plus the three means (gift, penance, knowledge) with their fruits; it addresses householder and renouncer alike.
The four are taken from the four அன்றோ clauses; the syntax is dense.
The verse speaks of birth (பிறக்குங் குடி) by denying that a good woman's worth follows her family; tagged caste as a statement about birth rank, though it states no ranking rule.
The six are the riches of the one who fed the great ascetics with ghee and becomes like Vaisravana.
Counted by the three இனிது; the third, renouncing when the house fails, addresses the renouncer, but the verse is framed on household life.
Two items concern kings and two everyone; the tie is resolved to all because the verse's point, in its last item, is general.
